results.title: Federated Learning with Differential Privacy: An Utility-Enhanced Approach
results.content: In order to successfully avoid data leakage, adopting differential privacy (DP) in the local optimization process or in the local update aggregation process has emerged as two feasible ways for achieving sample-level or user-level privacy guarantees respectively, in federated learning models. To improve the privacy-utility trade-off, we present a modification to these vanilla differentially private algorithms based on a Haar wavelet transformation step and a novel noise injection scheme that significantly lowers the asymptotic bound of the noise variance. This algorithm is called differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD) and is considered highly effective in achieving sample-level differential privacy in FL applications. We propose a novel modification to the DP-SGD and DP-FedAvg algorithms by employing a Haar wavelet transform approach to achieve a better utility-to-privacy tradeoff than their vanilla counterparts (i.e., ensuring the same DP guarantees for much better utility). We demonstrate how our method can be modified to improve utility in user-level DP configurations, specifically by introducing a wavelet transformation function to perform noise injection at the DP-FedAvg algorithm’s global aggregation step. Assume that a vanilla DP-SGD or DP-FedAvg algorithm using any accountant technique, such as the moments accountant [15] or the Renyi Differential Privacy (RDP) accountant [33], provides privacy guarantee when a noise with a variance of is introduced to gradients. These components collectively illustrate that the convergence rate of the DP-FedAvg via Wavelets algorithm is influenced by the learning rate, gradient dissimilarity, differential privacy noise, and the weighted contribution of local gradients. In order to minimize this deterioration, our proposed algorithm DP-FedAvg-WAV saves a factor of in the noise variance added to the model gradients compared to its vanilla algorithm, resulting in superior convergence performance. In the sample-level privacy setting, we use Dyn-DP-SGD, where the noise added to the gradients is adapted dynamically based on the sensitivity of the data. In the large noise setting, our method shows a 16.33% increase in accuracy compared to vanilla DP-FedAvg and a 5.94% increase compared to Dyn-DP-FedAvg. results.content: # Privacy, accuracy, and model fairness trade-offs in federated learning. As applications of machine learning become increasingly widespread, the need to ensure model accuracy and fairness while protecting the privacy of user data becomes more pronounced. In our approach, we seek to achieve an acceptable trade-off between privacy, accuracy, and model fairness by using differential privacy (DP), which also helps to minimize privacy risks by protecting the presence of a specific sample in the training data. Hence, we discuss the fairness and privacy effect of local DP and global DP when applied to federated learning by designing a fair and privacy quantification mechanism. In doing so, we can achieve an acceptable trade-off between accuracy, privacy, and model fairness. Is it feasible to improve the group fairness by applying differential privacy in the federated learning context? First, we apply two settings of differential privacy in a federated learning setting by training FL neural networks separately, using local DP and global DP, to evaluate the influence on fairness. The trade-off between fairness and privacy can be achieved using the differential privacy stochastic gradient descent algorithm (DP-SGD) proposed by Abadi et al., 2016 with an acceptable cost of accuracy. Section 2 reviews the existing fairness protection methods and related literature on fairness and privacy collaborative learning in the FL context. In this section, we introduce the key technologies that underpin the present study, including differential privacy (DP), DP in federated learning, and fairness metrics. The experiments with the benchmark LEAF conducted by Caldas et al., 2018 apply differential privacy federated learning models. * ### Fairness and privacy preserving in federated learning: A survey. The authors in [252] demonstrated that achieving a trade-off between privacy, accuracy, and model fairness is possible using differential privacy through careful privacy-parameter selection, such as choosing the appropriate noise scale and gradient clipping norm. In addition to providing an extensive review of the current literature on privacy and fairness issues, we also examine the existing approaches for achieving a balance between these two ethical notions to develop robust FL systems. His research interests include privacy preserving, AI fairness, and machine learning.
